title: Parables, Taxes, and The Greatest Commandment

questions.question: In the Parable of the Tenants, a man planted a vineyard and leased it to tenants. When he sent a servant to get some of the fruit, what did the tenants do?
options: They took him and beat him and sent him away empty-handed
They paid him fully the share owed
They immediately killed him with swords
They trapped him in a pit
questions.correctAnswer: They took him and beat him and sent him away empty-handed
questions.explanation: Mark 12:3 (ESV): "And they took him and beat him and sent him away empty-handed."

questions.question: After the master of the vineyard had numerous servants beaten and killed, he had one left to send: a beloved son. What did the tenants say when they saw the son?
options: "This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours."
"The master finally respects us. Let us negotiate a new lease."
"Let us seize him and ransom him back to the master."
"We must flee, for he will surely bring soldiers with him."
questions.correctAnswer: "This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours."
questions.explanation: Mark 12:7 (ESV): "But those tenants said to one another, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.'"

questions.question: What did the tenants do to the beloved son?
options: They took him and killed him and threw him out of the vineyard
They scourged him with whips and sent him back bleeding
They crucified him upon a tree inside the vineyard walls
They tied him up and starved him in the watchtower
questions.correctAnswer: They took him and killed him and threw him out of the vineyard
questions.explanation: Mark 12:8 (ESV): "And they took him and killed him and threw him out of the vineyard."

questions.question: Jesus quoted an Old Testament scripture after the parable: "The stone that the builders rejected has become..." what?
options: The cornerstone
The capstone
The foundation rock
A stumbling block
questions.explanation: Mark 12:10 (ESV): "Have you not read this Scripture: 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone;'"

questions.question: The Jewish leaders sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to trap Jesus in his talk. What did they ask Him concerning taxes?
options: "Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not? Should we pay them, or should we not?"
"If we pay taxes to Rome, do we have to pay the temple tax?"
"Whose taxes are meant for God, and whose are meant for Caesar?"
"Why does your group not pay taxes as the rest of us do?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not? Should we pay them, or should we not?"
questions.explanation: Mark 12:14-15 (ESV): "Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not? Should we pay them, or should we not?"

questions.question: Jesus asked them to bring Him a denarius, and then asked: "Whose likeness and inscription is this?" Who did they say?
options: Caesar's
Augustus'
Tiberius
Pilate's
questions.explanation: Mark 12:16 (ESV): "And they brought one. And he said to them, 'Whose likeness and inscription is this?' They said to him, 'Caesar's.'"

questions.question: How did Jesus astound the Pharisees and Herodians with His answer regarding taxes?
options: "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's."
"Let the false coins belong to the idol worshipers, keep only shekels."
"A true servant gives everything to God and nothing to Caesar."
"Whatever your conscience tells you to do, do it."
questions.correctAnswer: "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's."
questions.explanation: Mark 12:17 (ESV): "Jesus said to them, 'Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's.' And they marveled at him."

questions.question: The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, asked Jesus a question about seven brothers who married the same woman. In the resurrection, whose wife would she be? What did Jesus teach about marriage in the resurrection?
options: "For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven."
"She will be married to the first brother, for he was the first husband."
"She will choose who she loves most among the seven."
"She will be married to none of them as punishment for barrenness."
questions.correctAnswer: "For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven."
questions.explanation: Mark 12:25 (ESV): "For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven."

questions.question: To prove that the dead are raised, Jesus recalled the story of Moses at the bush, where God said, "I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." What conclusion did Jesus state?
options: "He is not God of the dead, but of the living. You are quite wrong."
"Therefore, they are waiting for you in Paradise."
"And Moses knew then that the resurrection was true from the beginning."
"This means you should stop teaching false doctrines in the temple."
questions.correctAnswer: "He is not God of the dead, but of the living. You are quite wrong."
questions.explanation: Mark 12:27 (ESV): "He is not God of the dead, but of the living. You are quite wrong."

questions.question: One of the scribes came up and heard them disputing with Jesus, and asked Him: "Which commandment is the most important of all?" How did Jesus begin His famous answer?
options: "Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart..."
"Love the Lord your God, and do not worship carved images."
"Keep the Sabbath day holy, for it is the sign of the covenant."
"Honor your father and your mother so that your days may be long."
questions.correctAnswer: "Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart..."
questions.explanation: Mark 12:29-30 (ESV): "Jesus answered, 'The most important is, "Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one. And you shall love the Lord your God..."'"

questions.question: What is the second most important commandment according to Jesus?
options: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
"Do not steal from your neighbor."
"Be merciful just as your Father is merciful."
"Forgive those who trespass against you."
questions.correctAnswer: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
questions.explanation: Mark 12:31 (ESV): "The second is this: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.' There is no other commandment greater than these."

questions.question: How did the scribe respond to Jesus' answer about the greatest commandments?
options: He agreed, stating that loving God and neighbor is much more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices
He argued heavily, stating the Sabbath was greater
He scoffed, asking how Jesus, a carpenter, could know the law
He walked away silently, deep in thought
questions.correctAnswer: He agreed, stating that loving God and neighbor is much more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices
questions.explanation: Mark 12:33 (ESV): "...and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is much more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices."

questions.question: While teaching in the temple, Jesus asked how the scribes can say that the Christ is the son of David, quoting David saying, "The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand..." What was Jesus implying?
options: "David himself calls him Lord. So how is he his son?"
"David knew that the Christ would not be from his lineage at all."
"The Son of David does not need to rule from Jerusalem."
"David means that the Christ is merely a man, a son of man."
questions.correctAnswer: "David himself calls him Lord. So how is he his son?"
questions.explanation: Mark 12:37 (ESV): "David himself calls him Lord. So how is he his son?' And the great throng heard him gladly."

questions.question: Jesus warned the crowds, "Beware of the scribes," pointing out that they devour widows' houses and for a pretense do what?
options: "Make long prayers"
"Wear elaborate phylacteries"
"Fasts visibly with gloomy faces"
"Sacrifice many expensive animals"
questions.explanation: Mark 12:40 (ESV): "who devour widows' houses and for a pretense make long prayers. They will receive the greater condemnation."

questions.question: After watching the rich put large sums into the offering box, Jesus watched a poor widow put in two small copper coins. What did He declare about her?
options: "Truly, I say to you, this poor widow has put in more than all those who are contributing to the offering box."
"Her money is cursed because she did not pay tithes earlier."
"She has purchased her eternal life fully this day."
"Let her be given more bread than the scribes in the morning."
questions.correctAnswer: "Truly, I say to you, this poor widow has put in more than all those who are contributing to the offering box."
questions.explanation: Mark 12:43-44 (ESV): "...he said to them, 'Truly, I say to you, this poor widow has put in more than all those who are contributing... she out of her poverty has put in everything she had...'"

key_verse_text: "And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength. The second is this: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.' There is no other commandment greater than these."
